win_win_seeking.reason: Win-win seeking treats disputes as shared problems to solve cooperatively, which overlaps with working together for shared goals though it is specific to negotiation.

accommodating.reason: Accommodating means adjusting one's positions to meet others' needs, which shares the willingness to give up own stance for the group's cooperation.

individualistic.reason: Individualistic emphasis on self-reliance and autonomy over group norms is the reverse of putting group goals ahead of one's own priorities.

agreeable.reason: Agreeableness prioritizes harmony, cooperation and finding common ground, which overlaps with a team player's cooperative spirit but is about interpersonal tone rather than work.

selfish.reason: Selfishness puts one's own interests above others, the opposite of a team player setting aside own priorities for the group.

competitive.reason: Competitiveness frames situations as contests to win against others, which is the opposite of cooperative teamwork toward shared goals.

unhelpful.reason: Unhelpfulness is indifference to others' needs and refusal to assist, the reverse of working cooperatively to get shared work done.

altruistic.reason: Altruism means putting the common good before personal gain and helping at cost to oneself, closely matching the team player's sacrificing own priorities for the group.

label: uncaring
gloss: This means being indifferent to how others feel and whether they fare well, showing no concern for their emotions or welfare and never adjusting one's conduct to spare them distress.

label: unctuous
gloss: This means speaking with an oily, excessive smoothness, piling on flattery and fawning compliments to win favor from those one wants something from.

sonnet.reason: Both involve excessive flattery to win favor from someone, but unctuous stresses oily, smooth manner of speech while sycophantic stresses excessive agreement and withholding honest feedback, so they share a core with different emphases.

opus.reason: Both centre on excessive flattery to win favour, but unctuous stresses an oily, smooth manner of speaking, while sycophantic stresses agreeing and giving up honest feedback to be liked.

sonnet.reason: Both involve smooth, polished speech, but unctuous is insincere flattery aimed at winning favor, while eloquent is skilled, graceful expression with no flattery or ulterior motive implied.
Both involve flattering people to gain advantage, but sly also covers rule-breaking, self-interest and entitlement, while unctuous is specifically about oily, fawning speech.
Both involve insincere praise to win favor; unctuous adds an oily, fawning manner and a self-serving motive, while flattering is more general and can also smooth social awkwardness.

opus.reason: Both are insincere praise used to win favor, and unctuous is the same flattery carried to an oily, fawning excess.

sonnet.reason: Both involve smooth, insincere talk meant to please, but unctuous centers on fawning flattery to win favor, while glib centers on ready, easy answers and charm without necessarily flattering or seeking something.

Both involve insincere social performance, but unctuous is specifically excessive flattery to win favor, while phony is broader false self-presentation (warmth, interest, expertise) without needing flattery or ulterior motive.

honest_humble_hexaco.reason: Honest-humble is about dealing straight, avoiding gain-seeking and claiming no special standing, which is the reverse of the candidate's oily, fawning manipulation.

sly_hexaco.reason: Sly shares the core of flattering people to get what one wants and gaming rules for gain, matching the candidate's self-interested fawning.

flirty.reason: Flirty concerns playful romantic or sexual banter, while unctuous is about oily flattery to win favor; they share only the general area of charming speech.

candid.reason: Candid means telling people honest assessments, flaws included, which is the opposite of the candidate's excessive flattery.

flattering.reason: Flattering means lavishing praise to win favor, which is a core part of the candidate's excessive, fawning compliments.

sycophantic.reason: Sycophantic means excessively agreeing with and flattering someone to be liked, closely matching the candidate's fawning to win favor.

eloquent.reason: Eloquent praises fluent, graceful, persuasive language, whereas unctuous is an oily, excessive smoothness; both involve smooth speech but differ in quality and motive.

bombastic.reason: Bombastic is inflated, pompous language meant to impress, which overlaps with the candidate's excessive, showy manner but is about grandiosity rather than flattery.

glib.reason: Glib describes smooth, easy charm saying whatever goes down well without meaning it, sharing the candidate's insincere smoothness.

phony.reason: Phony means putting on false warmth or interest, which overlaps with the candidate's insincere fawning but is broader about presenting a false self.

verbose.reason: Verbose is being long-winded in speech and writing, a matter of length, which is unrelated to oily flattery.

concise.reason: Concise is brevity and directness, nothing about flattery or smoothness, so it is unrelated to the candidate's manner beyond the general area of speech.

chattering.reason: Chattering is talking on in a quick stream of small remarks, which concerns quantity of talk rather than oily flattery.

plain_spoken.reason: Plain-spoken is simple, unadorned direct language, the reverse of the candidate's ornate, oily smoothness.

label: unflappable
gloss: This means keeping one's composure and steady tone when things go wrong, so that pressure, setbacks or urgent demands never rush or rattle one's responses.
